title: Release mise-en-place (chef notes)
content:
Purpose: quick personal checklist + heuristics for next feature flip (model v2.1 -> v2.2) — lightweight, kitchen-style notes. Use as a rapid reference during late-stage rollout prep and the first 2 hours of live canary.

High level concept (mise en place):
- Prep everything you might need before flipping an ounce of traffic: telemetry queries, quick rollback commands, pinned versions, client toggle IDs, warmup cohorts.
- Taste test: small deterministic cohort to validate functionality + quality signals, then expand by geometric factor if health is stable.
- Service: maintain an observable slow ramp with guardrails and explicit pin-back thresholds.

Phased plan (quick):
1) Preparation (T-48h to T-1h)
   - Lock the canary spec: cohorts = [internal-internal, internal-external, 1% prod, 5% prod] (order matters).
   - Confirm model artifacts: model:v2.2-quant-fast, fallback path -> v2.1. Pin hashes in rollout config.
   - Create a warmup script: 500 synthetic short prompts + 200 long prompts targeted to common clients (messaging, search). Run on dedicated warmup pool.
   - Sanity checks: smoke test suite (5 critical prompts) passes locally and on staging.
   - Telemetry dashboards: open tabs for latency p95/p99, error budget burn, token cost delta, hallucination eval metric (prompt-suite-eval), user-signal rate (CTR-like metric for feature).

2) Taste (canary start)
   - Flip internal-internal (team users) — 1% of internal traffic, 0.1% of prod; wait 10 minutes.
   - Signals to watch in first 10 minutes: request error rate (>0.25% absolute increase), p95 latency (+>60 ms absolute or +30% relative), token cost per request (+>15% relative), model output regression score (auto-eval) drop >5 points.
   - Manual QA: 5-minute window for infra/product leads to run targeted checks (safety prompts, chargeback scenarios).
   - If stable -> expand to internal-external cohort (pilot customers) for 20 minutes.

3) Ramp (gradual production):
   - 1% prod -> 5% prod -> 15% prod -> 40% prod. Each step minimum observation window: 15m, 20m, 30m, 60m respectively.
   - For each step, require: error delta < 0.15% absolute, p95 delta < 40 ms or <20% relative, SLO alerts not firing, auto-eval quality stable.
   - If any threshold breached, trigger immediate pinback to v2.1 for affected cohort and open a fast incident channel.

Pinning and escape hatches:
- Pin command (CLI): rwdctl rollout pin --env=prod --model=v2.1 --scope=cohort:<cohort-id> (stash exact command in runbook).
- Fast rollback: route 100% of canary cohort traffic to fallback pool. Communicate to customer-facing slack channel.
- Soft pin: reduce traffic share by factor of 0.25 every 5 minutes instead of full rollback for transient pressure events.

Observability mapping (what to look at and why):
- p99 latency spike + token-cost delta -> likely kernel or memory pressure; check node-level GPU queues and OOM logs.
- p95 latency increase with constant p99 -> tail effect improved by batching; consider temporarily reducing batch windows.
- Error rate increase correlated with particular clients -> client SDK bug or input distribution shift; quarantine client cohort.
- Auto-eval drop for a subset of prompts -> content/regression issue; run debug eval on failing prompts, compare logits if available.

Telemetry quick-queries (placeholders to paste into dashboard):
- errors/1m by cohort (filter=canary)
- latency/p95,p99 by model_version and region
- tokens/req and cost/dollar by model_version
- autoeval.score by prompt_group and model_version

Warmup notes (critical):
- KV cache is cold for v2.2; warm up with synthetic sequences that mirror heavy clients. Focus on sequence lengths 32-512.
- Warmup concurrency: start with low concurrency to populate caches, then burst-run a second wave to validate throughput.
- Track cache-hit ratio (if available) and model init times per pod.

Quality safety heuristics (taste-test prompts):
- 12 targeted safety prompts (edge-case hallucination and safety trigger checks).
- 8 domain-specific prompts from top 3 clients (retain anonymized examples in secure doc).
- 5 regression-sensitive prompts (long dialogs where context retention matters).

Communication plan (short):
- Pre-rollout: announce in #release-prep channel 30m before start, include expected timeline and toggle IDs.
- On canary start: post initial status with link to dashboards and first 10m observation summary.
- On anomaly: open triage thread, tag SRE and product lead, recommend immediate pin or softback.

Open questions / TODOs (brain dump):
- How to automate soft pin scaling? Can we wire a runbook script to reduce cohort by 25% per 5m? (ticket?).
- Need a one-click button in Console for immediate model pin -> raise product ticket.
- Confirm which customers are in "internal-external" cohort; ensure CS is looped in and comfortable.
- Add a small synthetic eval that runs after each ramp step and posts a pass/fail to Slack.

Fallthrough checklist (if rollback occurs):
- Notify CS and account owners of affected customers within 10 minutes.
- Capture repro examples and attach to incident ticket.
- Start postmortem template and collect top 3 probable root causes.

Quick reference (cheat lines for my fingers):
- Pin: rwdctl rollout pin --env=prod --model=v2.1 --cohort=<id>
- Softback: rwdctl rollout scale --env=prod --cohort=<id> --factor=0.25
- Force route: rwdctl route set --env=prod --cohort=<id> --target=fallback-pool

Notes to self: keep this short during the run. Use the mise-en-place metaphor: if it isn't prepped, don't flip more traffic. Trust the signals, not the urge to finish fast.

End.
